intro: Zoom for UX researchers on Mac means the Zoom Workplace desktop app, version 7.2.5, released October 31, 2026. Use it to host moderated sessions, record them to your Mac, and sketch on a whiteboard during the call. This guide covers setup, recording, plan limits, whiteboards, and where Lazur helps while you run the session.
tldr: Use the Zoom Workplace desktop app on your Mac. Zoom says computer recording is not supported on iOS, iPad, or Android.
The free Basic plan allows local recording only, and group meetings end at 40 minutes.
Local recordings have no audio transcript. Keep the save folder on a local drive and don't sleep the Mac during conversion.
Whiteboards need an admin to switch them on, hold 200 MB each on most plans, and can't go to people without a Zoom account.
Lazur points at controls, answers out loud, dictates your notes, and sets timers. It does not click for you.

blocks.text: You probably run remote sessions in Zoom already. User Interviews calls Zoom a popular choice for remote UX research, and its State of User Research report mentions it more than 130 times. That count comes from a 2024 article, and it counts mentions, not users. This page covers the parts that trip people up on a Mac: the desktop app, local recording, whiteboards, and the limits on the free plan.
Install the Zoom desktop app on your Mac

Zoom's computer recording needs the desktop app. Zoom says it is not supported on iOS, iPad, or Android. The desktop app itself runs on Windows, macOS, and Linux. Lazur runs on Apple silicon and Intel Macs, so your chip is not the blocker.

The current macOS build is Zoom Workplace 7.2.5, build 90525, released October 31, 2026. Zoom's release notes list it that way. To check your copy, open the Zoom menu in the menu bar and choose Check for Updates. Update before your first session, not the morning of it.

items: Open the Zoom menu, choose Check for Updates, and install 7.2.5 or later.
Sign in with the account you will host with, so your plan settings apply.
Open Zoom > Settings and test the microphone and camera before anyone joins.

blocks.text: Choose a Zoom plan for user research

The free Basic plan allows group meetings up to 40 minutes, with up to 100 participants. It allows local recording only. Cloud recording needs a paid plan. Zoom's pricing page lists Pro at $16.99 per user per month billed monthly, or $14.16 billed annually. Business is $21.99 per user per month billed monthly, or $18.33 billed annually. Enterprise has no public price. Prices change, so check their pricing page before you buy.

blocks.text: Here is how the free plan plays out. Say a session needs more than 40 minutes, with observers on the call. The Basic plan ends the group meeting at the cap, and your local recording ends with it. Plan the session length to fit the cap, or move to a paid plan before you book. Don't find out at minute 40.
Record a Zoom session locally on your Mac

items: Start or join the meeting in the Zoom desktop app.
Click Record in the meeting controls toolbar.
If a menu appears, choose Record on this Computer.
Stop the recording from the same toolbar when the task or session ends.
Wait for conversion to finish before you close the lid or sleep the Mac.

blocks.text: Zoom saves video as MP4 and audio as M4A. It converts both files after the meeting ends. The file is not ready the moment you leave the call, so don't assume it is.

Two habits prevent most lost files. First, keep the save location on a local drive. Zoom advises against cloud-synced, external, and network folders, because they can cause conversion problems. Second, don't interrupt conversion. Zoom says restarting, sleeping the disk, or closing the laptop can corrupt local recordings beyond recovery. Plug in the charger for long sessions.

If the Record button never offers Record on this Computer, your admin may have it turned off. Admins can enable Record to computer files in the web portal under Account Management > Account Settings > Recording & Transcript. They can also lock the setting. Ask them before the study starts, not during the session.
Local or cloud recording for usability testing

Local recording is the only recording option on the free plan, so it matters. It has real gaps. Zoom says local recordings don't support audio transcription. They also can't capture active speaker, gallery view, and shared screen separately. For those, Zoom recommends cloud recording.

blocks.text: For a moderated usability test, local recording often covers what you need. You get one file with the screen and the faces together. That is enough to rewatch a task and check what the participant said. Take your own notes during the call, because the file won't give you a transcript. If you need one, decide before the session, not after.
Zoom Whiteboard for card sorts and workshops

Zoom Whiteboard works on Basic, Pro, Business, Education, and Enterprise accounts. An administrator has to turn on Zoom Whiteboard for the account first. During a meeting, open the Whiteboards button in the in-meeting controls and choose New Whiteboard. Each whiteboard holds up to 200 MB for most users, and up to 1 GB on Whiteboard Plus.

Two limits matter for research. You can't send a whiteboard to someone without a Zoom account, so plan how your participants get results. Image-heavy boards also reach the 200 MB limit sooner. Keep the board for live work. Move the final output into your research doc the same day.
How many participants for remote moderated usability testing

Nielsen Norman Group recommends five users per usability test for most projects. It says five people find almost as many problems as many more participants would. That advice is from a 2012 article. Treat it as a starting point, not a rule. NN/g also describes remote moderated testing as a live session, often run in a video conferencing app like Zoom.

Cost is the other question. NN/g's video on remote usability testing costs says an unmoderated study with five participants may be 20 to 40% cheaper than a moderated one. The exact cost varies. Moderated sessions cost more because you hold a live call with each person. Budget for the call time, setup, and the debrief after each session.
Common mistakes in Zoom usability testing on Mac

items: Recording into a cloud-synced folder, which can break file conversion.
Closing the laptop or sleeping the Mac while the file converts.
Assuming a local recording comes with a transcript. It doesn't.
Running past the 40-minute cap on Basic in the middle of a session.
Sending a whiteboard to a participant who has no Zoom account.
Pressing Record before you say so. Get consent out loud first.
Testing the microphone, camera, and recording for the first time during the session.

blocks.text: If the recording file is missing after a session

Check three things in order. First, confirm conversion finished, since Zoom converts files after the meeting ends. Second, open the save location in the Zoom desktop app and look for the MP4 or M4A file. Third, ask your admin whether Record to computer files is still on. If the file is still missing, write down what happened while it is fresh. Then contact Zoom support.
Check the recording before you rely on it

Open the file as soon as conversion finishes. Play a minute of it and confirm the audio is there and the screen is readable. Check that the length roughly matches the session you ran. A file that plays but is silent is still a lost session, so catch it early.

Say out loud when you start and stop recording. Write the file name in your session notes right away. That one line saves you from hunting for the file later, when the participant is gone and the notes are cold.
Lazur for Zoom voice help during sessions

Lazur is a voice assistant for the Mac that lives in the notch. Hold ⌥⌘, which is Option plus Command, and ask about anything on your screen. Lazur answers out loud. Ask where something is, and it draws a circle and a label around it. Ask how to do something, and it guides you one click at a time, waiting for each click. Lazur does not click for you.
Say you can't find the recording option mid-session. Hold ⌥⌘ and ask where Record is. Lazur circles the control and labels it. You click it yourself, and your eyes stay on the participant.

Lazur listens and looks only while you hold the shortcut. It doesn't follow the call in the background. Audio and the screenshot go to AI providers to answer, and they are not stored. Content is never used to train AI models. Lazur is not a plugin or add-in for Zoom, and it has no partnership with Zoom.
Dictate notes and set reminders during a session

Hold fn to dictate clean, formatted text at the cursor in any app. Dictation is included, and it is unlimited on Pro and Power. Add study names, product names like Zoom Workplace and Lazur, and participant codes to your personal dictionary. Then they come out spelled right. Snippets help too. Save your consent line as a snippet, so you can paste it before you press Record.

Timers and reminders are everyday tasks. Ask Lazur to set a timer for the think-aloud task, so the session stays on schedule. Ask it to add the debrief to Calendar, or a follow-up to Apple Reminders. Lazur handles timers, Apple Reminders, and Calendar events by voice.
Background research between UX sessions

Between sessions, you may need a method check. Ask Lazur to research a question, such as how NN/g recommends running remote moderated tests. Research runs in Lazur's own Chrome tabs, through the Lazur for Chrome extension. It comes back with a summary and a report. Open the sources yourself before you cite anything in a study plan.
Organize recordings and consent files

Make one folder per study. Keep it out of any cloud-synced folder while the file converts. Once conversion finishes, copy the MP4 or M4A file into the study folder, named with the session date and a participant code. Keep consent forms in the same folder, not in Downloads. If you track findings in a spreadsheet, see [Google Sheets for UX researchers on Mac](/for/ux-researchers/google-sheets).

Treat participant video as sensitive data. Limit who can open the folder, and delete raw files when your study plan says to. Keep the consent record beside them, so you can answer questions later. If your team keeps findings in Notion, the [Notion setup for UX researchers](/for/ux-researchers/notion) covers the database side.
Day before checklist for Zoom research sessions

items: Set the save location to a local drive, not a cloud-synced or network folder.
Ask your admin to confirm Record to computer files is on.
Check that the session fits your plan's group meeting limit.
Free up disk space on the Mac before the session.
Run a short test recording and open the file.
Save your consent line as a snippet, ready to read aloud.

blocks.text: When Zoom is not the right fit for your team

User Interviews lists four reasons teams look beyond video call tools: pricing, security, specific feature needs, and fit with an existing tech stack. If one of those blocks you, pilot a second tool with one session before you switch. Check its pricing page and your IT team's security rules first.

Try Lazur with the free trial. It needs no credit card, and it starts when you first open the app. Pricing for Pro and Power is on the [pricing page](/pricing). Get the app from the [download page](/download). For more on Zoom specifically, read [Lazur for Zoom on Mac](/apps/zoom).

faq.question: Can I record a Zoom meeting on a Mac for free?
faq.answer: Yes. The Basic plan allows local recording only. Click Record in the meeting controls toolbar, then choose Record on this Computer if a menu appears. Group meetings on Basic end at 40 minutes, so plan longer sessions around that cap or move to a paid plan.

faq.question: Where are local Zoom recordings saved on a Mac?
faq.answer: Zoom saves them to the local save location set in the Zoom desktop app. Check that location in the app's Settings before your session. Keep it on a local drive. Zoom advises against cloud-synced, external, or network folders because they can cause conversion problems.

faq.question: Does a local Zoom recording include a transcript?
faq.answer: No. Zoom says local recordings do not support audio transcription. Take your own notes during the call. If you need a transcript, check whether cloud recording fits your plan, since Zoom recommends cloud for some layouts.

faq.question: Why don't I see Record on this Computer in Zoom?
faq.answer: Your admin may have turned off Record to computer files. Admins can turn it on in the web portal under Account Management > Account Settings > Recording & Transcript, and they can lock the setting. Ask them before your study starts.

faq.question: How many participants should a usability test have?
faq.answer: Nielsen Norman Group recommends five users per usability test for most projects, and says five people find almost as many problems as many more would. That advice is from a 2012 article, so treat it as a starting point for your own study.

faq.question: Can I use Zoom Whiteboard on the free plan?
faq.answer: Zoom Whiteboard works on Basic and higher plans, but an administrator must turn it on for the account first. Each whiteboard holds up to 200 MB for most users. You can't send a whiteboard to someone who doesn't have a Zoom account.

faq.question: Can Lazur record my Zoom meeting or click buttons for me?
faq.answer: No. Lazur does not click buttons, edit files, or operate Zoom for you. It answers questions out loud, circles controls on your screen, and guides you one click at a time. It listens only while you hold the shortcut.

faq.question: Does Lazur plug into Zoom or add features to it?
faq.answer: No. Lazur is not a plugin or add-in for Zoom, and it has no partnership with Zoom. You use Zoom as normal, and you ask Lazur for help with the screen in front of you.
